from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        speedometer = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg")

        # Layout
        self.place_at_grid(pillar_a, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "C2", scale_factor=0.7)

        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "C5", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_in_area(bridge, "B3", "B4", scale_factor=0.75)
        self.place_in_area(label_bridge, "C3", "C4", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, "A3", scale_factor=0.5)

        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(pillar_a), FadeIn(label_a), FadeIn(speedometer))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF9900"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(pillar_b), FadeIn(label_b))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00CCFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(bridge), Write(label_bridge))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # Emphasis
        self.play(Flash(pillar_a, color="#FF9900"), Flash(pillar_b, color="#00CCFF"), Flash(bridge, color="#FFFFFF"), FadeIn(odometer.move_to(self.grid["F3"])))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The derivative of accumulation returns the original function.",
            "As the width expands, area increases instantly.",
            "This rate of change equals the function's height.",
            "Thus, F prime of x equals f of x.",
            "Area growth rate mirrors the function's current value."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem (Part 1)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        calc_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg")
        graph_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/graph.svg")
        
        # Mobjects
        theorem_text = Text("Fundamental Theorem", color=WHITE)
        integral_expr = MathTex(r"\\int_a^x f(t) dt", color="#00CCFF")
        derivative_expr = MathTex(r"\\frac{d}{dx} F(x) = f(x)", color="#FF9900")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(theorem_text, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(calc_icon, 'B2', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(theorem_text), FadeIn(calc_icon))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00CCFF"))
        self.place_in_area(integral_expr, 'C3', 'C5', scale_factor=0.75)
        self.play(Write(integral_expr))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF9900"))
        self.place_in_area(derivative_expr, 'D3', 'D5', scale_factor=0.75)
        self.play(Write(derivative_expr))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(derivative_expr))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF9900"))
        self.place_at_grid(graph_icon, 'E4', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(graph_icon), Circumscribe(derivative_expr))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Practical Application: Calculating Net Change", [
            "The integral equals the anti-derivative difference.",
            "F of b minus F of a gives net change.",
            "Anti-derivatives unlock simple area calculation."
        ])

        # Load SVG assets
        # Path references from storyboard:
        # /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/graph.svg
        # /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/curve.svg
        
        graph_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/graph.svg")
        curve_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/curve.svg")
        
        # Define Manim objects for the graph
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"color": WHITE})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x * (4 - x) + 0.5, color="#00CCFF")
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0.5, 3.5], color="#FF9900", opacity=0.5)
        
        # Grouped graph object for placement
        graph = VGroup(axes, curve, area, graph_icon, curve_icon)
        
        # Apply layout based on feedback
        # Initial placement to avoid encroachment and provide balance
        self.place_in_area(graph, 'A2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.65)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00CCFF"))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), FadeIn(graph_icon))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF9900"))
        self.play(FadeIn(area), FadeIn(curve_icon))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF66"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The Inverse Relationship", [
            "Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.",
            "They form a closed, powerful logical loop.",
            "Calculus turns infinite sums into algebraic steps."
        ])
        
        # Define icons
        # Note: Storyboard references assets but provides non-existent files. Using MathTex placeholders as original code.
        diff_icon = MathTex(r"\\frac{d}{dx}", color="#FF9900", font_size=72)
        int_icon = MathTex(r"\\int", color="#00CCFF", font_size=72)
        formula_group = VGroup(diff_icon, int_icon).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        
        # Define loop
        arc_path = Arc(radius=0.7, start_angle=0, angle=PI, color=WHITE)
        sum_algebra_label = Text("Sum -> Algebra", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF9900"))
        self.place_in_area(formula_group, 'C3', 'D4', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(diff_icon), Write(int_icon))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # They form a closed, powerful logical loop.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00CCFF"))
        self.place_in_area(arc_path, 'C3', 'C5', scale_factor=0.85)
        self.play(Create(arc_path))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Calculus turns infinite sums into algebraic steps.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(sum_algebra_label, 'E4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(sum_algebra_label))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: The Bridge Between Slopes and Areas

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Two Pillars
sections.content: Briefly recap derivatives as the 'slope of a tangent' (instantaneous change) and integrals as the 'area under a curve' (accumulation). Use a visualization of a moving car: speedometer (derivative) vs. odometer (integral).
sections.example: A squirrel running: The speed graph shows how fast it moves at time 't', while the integral shows total distance covered.

sections.title: The Conceptual Paradox
sections.content: Pose the question: Why should the process of finding a slope be related to the process of finding an area? Introduce the 'Accumulation Function' F(x) = ∫[a to x] f(t)dt, representing the growing area under a curve.
sections.example: Imagine a 2D printer head moving across a page; the 'area' fills up as the head moves, linking the rate of movement (f) to the accumulated ink (F).

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem (Part 1)
sections.content: Visually demonstrate that the derivative of the accumulation function returns the original function: F'(x) = f(x). Use an animation where a rectangle's height changes as its width 'dx' expands, showing the instantaneous change in area equals the function height.
sections.example: As a robotic arm traces a mountain silhouette, the rate at which the shaded area beneath it increases is exactly equal to the current height of the mountain at that specific point.

sections.title: Practical Application: Calculating Net Change
sections.content: Connect the theorem to evaluation: ∫[a to b] f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a). Explain that to find the area, we simply need the 'anti-derivative'—the inverse of a derivative.
sections.example: Calculating the total weight gain of a bear over a season by integrating its daily weight-gain rate function from Spring to Autumn.

sections.title: Summary: The Inverse Relationship
sections.content: Synthesize the lesson: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations, like addition and subtraction or multiplication and division. Reiterate that this relationship turns difficult infinite summations into simple algebraic evaluations.
sections.example: Visual transition: A 'differentiation arrow' pointing one way and an 'integration arrow' pointing back, forming a closed logical loop.
